title: For q>1 and c>0, the nonstandard quantum complex projective-line C*-algebra is the pullback of two Toeplitz algebras along their common symbol map
author: Nicola Ciccoli; Albert Jeu-Liang Sheu
source_version: Official SIGMA 16 (2020) article 073, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2020.073; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-09-30, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
difficulty_reason: The substantive obligation is to recover the entire quantum homogeneous-space algebra from its concrete operator family, rather than identify a quotient or only a fixed representation. The author constructs two separate compact-operator ideals from defect projections, derives the double weighted-shift decomposition and controls the possible unitary remainder by its invariant spectrum. A final parameter-removing change of basis completes the faithful pullback realization; this is beyond standard qualifying operator theory.

retained_original_metadata.statement_scope: Exactly the n=1 nonstandard quantum projective-line algebra of Section2, c>0 and q>1: C(CP^1_{q,c}) is isomorphic to C*({X1*X2,X1*X1}) with X1=sqrt(c)alpha+gamma and X2=-q^-1 sqrt(c)gamma+alpha*, and to {(T,S) in Toeplitz direct-sum Toeplitz: sigma(T)=sigma(S)}. The entire circle-parameter family is covered by Section4; no higher-dimensional quantum projective space is claimed.
